review_note: Injective objects in abelian sheaves remain injective as abelian presheaves. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
Write $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ for abelian sheaves and $\mathrm{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ for abelian presheaves on the same site $\mathcal C$; the former embeds in the latter by forgetting the sheaf condition. No assumption from the preceding presheaf section is inherited.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. An injective abelian sheaf is also injective as an
object in the category $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site.
$\mathcal I$ is an injective object of $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$.
conclusions: $\mathcal I$ is injective in the abelian category $\mathrm{PAb}(\mathcal C)$.

review_note: Injective abelian sheaf I is Čech-acyclic for each site cover, and its degree-zero Čech group is I(U). Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$, the Čech cohomology $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ is cohomology of the complex of compatible products of sections on iterated fibre products. The word injective refers to injectivity in the **sheaf** category $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective abelian sheaf, i.e., an injective
object of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.
Then
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathcal{I}(U) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site and $\mathcal U$ is a covering of an object $U$.
$\mathcal I$ is injective as an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\cong\mathcal I(U)$ and $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-trivial-cech}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective abelian sheaf, i.e., an injective
object of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.
Then
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathcal{I}(U) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$

review_note: For each cover there is a natural morphism from the Čech cochain complex to derived sections, inducing Čech-to-sheaf cohomology maps. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For a site $\mathcal C$, a covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$, and an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$, let $\check{\mathcal C}^{\bullet}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ be the Čech complex and $R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$ the derived functor of sections over $U$ in $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$. The displayed map is a natural transformation to the derived category $D^+(\mathbf Z)$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
There is a transformation
$$
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, -)
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(U, -)
$$
of functors
$\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to D^{+}(\mathbf{Z})$.
In particular this gives a transformation of functors
$\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) \to H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$ for
$\mathcal{F}$ ranging over $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site, and $\mathcal U$ a covering of an object $U$.
conclusions: There is a natural transformation of functors $\check{\mathcal C}^{\bullet}(\mathcal U,-)\to R\Gamma(U,-)$ from $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ to $D^+(\mathbf Z)$.
For each abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ and $p\ge0$, this induces the natural comparison map $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to H^p(U,\mathcal F)$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-cohomology}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
There is a transformation
$$
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, -)
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(U, -)
$$
of functors
$\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to D^{+}(\mathbf{Z})$.
In particular this gives a transformation of functors
$\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) \to H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$ for
$\mathcal{F}$ ranging over $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.

review_note: Čech H¹→sheaf H¹ is injective and identifies classes of torsors trivialized on the specified covering. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
The comparison homomorphism $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to H^1(U,\mathcal G)$ is that of sites-cohomology.tex:1360–1375. On the slice site $\mathcal C/U$, a $\mathcal G|_U$-torsor is a sheaf of sets with a locally nonempty, simply transitive action by $\mathcal G|_U$, and the torsor is **trivial on $U_i$** when its restriction to $\mathcal C/U_i$ has a global section.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be an abelian sheaf
on $\mathcal{C}$. Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a
covering of $\mathcal{C}$. The map
$$
\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{G})
\longrightarrow
H^1(U, \mathcal{G})
$$
is injective and identifies $\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{G})$ via
the bijection of Lemma \ref{lemma-torsors-h1}
with the set of isomorphism classes of $\mathcal{G}|_U$-torsors
which restrict to trivial torsors over each $U_i$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site and $\mathcal G$ an abelian sheaf on it.
$\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$ is a covering in $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: The comparison $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to H^1(U,\mathcal G)$ is injective.
Its image corresponds under degree-one torsor classification to isomorphism classes of $\mathcal G|_U$-torsors trivial after restriction to every $U_i$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-h1}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be an abelian sheaf
on $\mathcal{C}$. Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a
covering of $\mathcal{C}$. The map
$$
\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{G})
\longrightarrow
H^1(U, \mathcal{G})
$$
is injective and identifies $\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{G})$ via
the bijection of Lemma \ref{lemma-torsors-h1}
with the set of isomorphism classes of $\mathcal{G}|_U$-torsors
which restrict to trivial torsors over each $U_i$.

review_note: The sheaf-to-presheaf inclusion is left exact and its higher right-derived functors are the presheaves U↦H^p(U,F). Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
Let $i:\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ be the forgetful inclusion of abelian sheaves as abelian presheaves. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$, define the abelian presheaf $\underline H^p(\mathcal F)$ by $U\mapsto H^p(U,\mathcal F)$, with restriction maps induced by site morphisms.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Consider the functor
$i : \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})$.
It is a left exact functor with right derived functors given by
$$
R^pi(\mathcal{F}) = \underline{H}^p(\mathcal{F}) :
U \longmapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})
$$
see discussion in Section \ref{section-locality}.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site.
$i$ is the inclusion of abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves.
conclusions: Its right derived functors satisfy $(R^pi)(\mathcal F)=\underline H^p(\mathcal F)$ for $p\ge0$, functorially in the abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-include}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Consider the functor
$i : \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})$.
It is a left exact functor with right derived functors given by
$$
R^pi(\mathcal{F}) = \underline{H}^p(\mathcal{F}) :
U \longmapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})
$$
see discussion in Section \ref{section-locality}.

review_note: The Čech-to-derived spectral sequence has E₂^{p,q}=Čech H^p(U,H^q(F)) and converges to ordinary H^{p+q}(U,F). Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ and $q\ge0$, write $\underline H^q(\mathcal F)$ for the abelian presheaf $V\mapsto H^q(V,\mathcal F)$ with natural restriction maps. For a covering $\mathcal U$, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$ is Čech cohomology of this presheaf.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$. For any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there
is a spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(U, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site and $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$ is a covering.
$\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: There is a spectral sequence with $E_2^{p,q}=\check H^p(\mathcal U,\underline H^q(\mathcal F))$ converging to $H^{p+q}(U,\mathcal F)$.
The spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal F$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-spectral-sequence}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$. For any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there
is a spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(U, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

review_note: Cohomology acyclicity on every finite multiple overlap of the cover forces equality of Čech and sheaf cohomology in all degrees. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For each multi-index $(i_0,\dots,i_p)$, the object $U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{i_p}$ is the iterated fibre product in the site, and its cohomology is taken with coefficients in the restriction of $\mathcal F$. For a sheaf $\mathcal F$, the Čech and derived-site cohomology groups are connected by the natural comparison map.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering.
Let $\mathcal{F} \in \Ob(\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}))$.
Assume that $H^i(U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$
for all $i > 0$, all $p \geq 0$ and all $i_0, \ldots, i_p \in I$.
Then $\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site and $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering.
$\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf.
For all $q>0$, $p\ge0$, and multi-indices $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)$, $H^q(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{i_p},\mathcal F)=0$.
conclusions: For all $p\ge0$, the canonical comparison $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-spectral-sequence-application}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering.
Let $\mathcal{F} \in \Ob(\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}))$.
Assume that $H^i(U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$
for all $i > 0$, all $p \geq 0$ and all $i_0, \ldots, i_p \in I$.
Then $\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$.

review_note: A cofinal system of coverings with Čech H¹(F)=0 makes G(U)→H(U) surjective for a short exact sheaf sequence. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
A *cofinal system of coverings* of $U$ is a collection such that every covering of $U$ admits a refinement by a member of the collection. Here $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ uses the Čech complex for the indicated covering, and short exactness is in the abelian sheaf category.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H} \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$. If there exists a cofinal system
of coverings $\mathcal{U}$ of $U$ such that
$\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$,
then the map $\mathcal{G}(U) \to \mathcal{H}(U)$ is
surjective.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site and $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal H\to0$ is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves.
$U$ is an object possessing a cofinal family of coverings $\mathcal U$ with $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$.
conclusions: The section map $\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal H(U)$ is surjective.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ses-cech-h1}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{H} \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$. If there exists a cofinal system
of coverings $\mathcal{U}$ of $U$ such that
$\check{H}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$,
then the map $\mathcal{G}(U) \to \mathcal{H}(U)$ is
surjective.

review_note: Vanishing Čech H^p over a cofinal system of covers on a basis closed under all cover overlaps implies ordinary higher cohomology vanishing there. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
Let $\mathrm{Cov}_{\mathcal C}$ be the set of covering families in the site $\mathcal C$. Assume $\mathcal B$ is a collection of objects and $\mathrm{Cov}$ a selected subset of covering families. Cofinal means every covering of an object $U\in\mathcal B$ is refined by one from $\mathrm{Cov}$ with target $U$. No extra assumptions are inherited from the preceding lemma.

(Variant of Cohomology, Lemma \ref{cohomology-lemma-cech-vanish}.)
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$ be the set
of coverings of $\mathcal{C}$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-site}). Let
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$,
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ we have
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$ and any $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site, $\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf, $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathrm{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathrm{Cov}\subseteq\mathrm{Cov}_{\mathcal C}$.
Every selected covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has $U$, all $U_i$, and all finite iterated fibre products among the $U_i$ in $\mathcal B$.
Selected coverings of every $U\in\mathcal B$ are cofinal among all coverings of $U$.
For every selected covering, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p>0$.
conclusions: $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$ and every $p>0$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-vanish-collection}
(Variant of Cohomology, Lemma \ref{cohomology-lemma-cech-vanish}.)
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$ be the set
of coverings of $\mathcal{C}$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-site}). Let
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$,
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ we have
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$ and any $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
